findings.message: The goal says the cap-blocking declined quarantines must become releasable and that every resolution kind has a reachable release path. The diff makes `release` accept `declined`, but the only engine consumer, clutch/stages.py:1370-1373, still computes `fix` only for `resolution.kind == "ticket"` and calls `flake.release` only after a merge event. No engine path ever passes `GreenRerunEvidence(..., f"declined:{box_id}", ...)`. The five declined quarantines (000359, 000449, 000450, 000451, 000457) stay active, and `detect` keeps escalating 'quarantine-cap crossed'. The criteria are met only in unit tests while the real code path differs. The boundary contract lists the callers of `Flake.release` as consumers, but clutch/stages.py is not in `## Scope fence`.
findings.paved_road: Add clutch/stages.py (and the test that covers the Check release loop) to `## Scope fence`. Have Check call `flake.release` for a declined resolution with a passing observation whose `fix_stem` is `declined:<box_id>`. Add an acceptance criterion that exercises the Check path.

findings.message: The added text "Check releases a passing quarantined test when its resolved fix has merged. A supplied green rerun also releases a report resolved as declined." sits in the Check paragraph and implies Check releases declined reports. Check (clutch/stages.py:1371) never does, so the doc describes behavior the code does not have.
findings.paved_road: Once Check calls release for declined reports (see the stages.py finding), keep the sentence. Until then, state that only a direct `Flake.release` call with a green rerun releases a declined report.

findings.message: Stale doc: line 503 still says "Check quarantines unedited fail-then-pass tests and releases them after a merged fix and a passing observation." It does not mention the declined release path this diff adds.
findings.paved_road: Update the line 503 bullet in the same change so it also describes the declined-report release (no merge, green rerun with fix_stem `declined:<box_id>`).
